cve_summary: In OpenJPEG 2.3.1, there is excessive iteration in the opj_t1_encode_cblks function of openjp2/t1.c. Remote attackers could leverage this vulnerability to cause a denial of service via a crafted bmp file. This issue is similar to CVE-2018-6616.
commit_message:
convertbmp: detect invalid file dimensions early

width/length dimensions read from bmp headers are not necessarily
valid. For instance they may have been maliciously set to very large
values with the intention to cause DoS (large memory allocation, stack
overflow). In these cases we want to detect the invalid size as early
as possible.

This commit introduces a counter which verifies that the number of
written bytes corresponds to the advertized width/length.

See commit 8ee335227bbc for details.

Signed-off-by: Young Xiao <YangX92@hotmail.com>
docstring:
"""
Summary: 
Reads RLE4 encoded bitmap data from a file and decodes it into a specified data buffer.

Parameters: 
IN (FILE*): Pointer to the input file stream containing the bitmap data.
pData (OPJ_UINT8*): Pointer to the buffer where the decoded pixel data will be stored.
stride (OPJ_UINT32): The number of bytes in a row of the image data.
width (OPJ_UINT32): The width of the image in pixels.
height (OPJ_UINT32): The height of the image in pixels.

Returns: 
OPJ_BOOL: Returns OPJ_TRUE if the data was read and written successfully, otherwise OPJ_FALSE.

Logic: 
The function processes the input file byte by byte, handling both encoded and absolute modes of RLE4 data. It decodes pixel values into the provided buffer while managing the image dimensions. If the number of written pixels does not match the expected size, it issues a warning and returns OPJ_FALSE.
